# Workspace Rules

## Authority & conduct
- Treat Adrian's explicit request as authority for all reversible in-scope work.
- Ask only for missing private input, new spend, unrequested publication or production mutation, destructive action, or a reserved decision.
- Finish requested work or report one hard blocker with exact missing input.
- Use primary checkout and current branch; create no branch or worktree without Adrian.
- Preserve user changes and never revert unrelated work.
- Lead with outcome and keep routine replies brief without forced closing filler.
- Never fabricate quotes, statistics, testimonials, stories, or evidence.
- Let Adrian approve visual output after opening the real artifact.
- For bounded plans, declare low/likely/high ETA and hard ceilings for files, bytes, lines, and active seconds.

## Bootstrap & toolchains
- After clone, pull, or any missing command, run `python3 tools/setup-workspace.py` on Mac or `py -3.11 tools\setup-workspace.py` on Windows.
- Install no workspace toolchain ad hoc; run setup, then `workspace-doctor`.
- Treat nearest `packageManager`, `engines`, and `rust-toolchain.toml` as authoritative.
- Use Node 26.5.x and pnpm 11.18.0 only when a repository has no stronger pin.
- Use pnpm in pnpm repositories; run package CLIs through `pnpm exec` rather than npm or npx.
- Use `python3` on Mac and `py -3.11` on Windows unless a repository venv says otherwise.
- Use the repository Rust toolchain; otherwise run Rust through `rustup stable`.
- Launch no visible Windows console for background automation.

## Mandatory systems
- Use Crypt for durable memory through installed shims; never discover it by hunting tokens or ports.
- Treat Crypt runtime storage as memory truth and Markdown as an export.
- Honor Membrane packets and report typed degraded state without claiming stronger enforcement.
- Use Sentinel assess through close for architecture, more than two changed files, non-obvious debugging, repeated failures, and signoff.
- Let rhook enforce Brief, Minimize, model caps, and safety guards; debug a gate instead of bypassing it.
- Run `tools/pipelines/hooks/status.py` when context or hooks are unhealthy.
- Run the matching thread guard before substantial work.
- At CRITICAL, use a fresh task unless Adrian explicitly directs this task to continue after seeing the result.

## Access
- Read `docs/rules/README.md` and matching runbook before remote, credentialed, or paid work.
- Use `ssh vendure-auto` for agent access to Hetzner.
- Use `win "<command>"` from Mac and `ssh mac "<command>"` from Windows.
- Read `docs/rules/github-access.md` before GitHub writes or pushes.
- Read `docs/rules/cloudflare-access.md` before Cloudflare, R2, Worker, DNS, or Pages work.
- Read `docs/rules/paid-compute.md` before metered compute.
- Never print or inspect credentials to discover configuration.

## Right Suite releases
- Use RightKit `right-release` from the primary checkout with manifest-pinned pnpm.
- Select explicit `patch` or `update` tier and keep build or seal separate from upload.
- Read release, signing, distribution, and licensing runbooks before release work.
- Upload or publish only when Adrian's current request names the exact build.
- Upload no test artifact.

## Scope & completion
- Read repository overlay before editing a nested repository.
- Load `/brand <code>` before brand or content work.
- Keep product facts, procedures, incident narratives, credentials topology, and current state outside this core.
- Add a rule only after repeated failure and keep it to one imperative plus one pointer.
- Use one instruction per bullet, one stable term per concept, and active voice where natural.
- Run focused checks first, then broader verification proportional to blast radius.
- Do not call work complete without concrete behavior or artifact evidence.

# Citadel Rules

## Purpose
Citadel is a private control room for live local Codex and Claude sessions.
Keep provider execution, credentials, and hidden session state on the enrolled machine.

## Canonical sources
- Read `README.md` for product and operator behavior.
- Read `docs/architecture.md` for components, flows, and security boundaries.
- Read `HANDOVER.md` before continuing active implementation work.
- Treat `STATUS.md` as current state, not a permanent rule source.

## Commands
- Run `cargo test --workspace` for Rust protocol, store, and node coverage.
- Run `cd packages/hub && node --test src/*.test.mjs` for hub coverage.
- Run `git diff --check` before handoff.

## Locked invariants
- Keep provider keys off the hub and load node tokens from environment or owner-only files.
- Keep enrollment on the SSH-operated CLI instead of exposing a public HTTP route.
- Persist deliveries before dispatch and prevent terminal replay after reconnect.
- Let nodes read only rooms where they hold a seat.
- Keep approval verdicts with the operator rather than the local Claude IPC channel.
- Preserve the outbound node connection and owner-only local socket model.

## Verification
- Run focused protocol or store tests before the full Rust and hub suites.
- Verify real session adapters against actual Codex app-server or Claude MCP behavior when changed.
- Require live deployment evidence before claiming persistence or remote-control acceptance.
